# Owner directives (highest priority; supersede roadmap/CI/portability wording)

1. **macOS only initially.** Apple Silicon, macOS 13+. No Linux or Windows code, CI jobs, runners, shims, packaging or portability work until the owner lifts this.
2. Keep platform code isolated behind `platform/` interfaces (clean seams only; no stubs or ports for other OSes).
3. CI/dev scripts target macOS only. Skip any roadmap item for Linux/Windows (M11, M12) and cross-platform CI matrices.

4. **Full Rust port, owner direction2026-10-14.** Stop the former C implementation queue. Port all first-party application/platform/UI/parser/raster/document/animation/MCP code and in-repo development/test tooling to Rust, then complete the existing product finish line. This supersedes the C17 language/build lock and the former two-implementation-worker ceiling. Use as many useful disjoint Luna codex exec workers as available allowance/resources permit; preserve one writer per module and coordinator-only shared integration. Existing subscription allowance only, no extra credits/API billing. Preserve the current C code, unfinished candidates and evidence as migration references; no delete/reset or false completion claim. macOS13+ AppleSilicon, MPL2, custom UI, owned source-preserving SVG/XML parser/rasterizer, minimal reviewed/pinned dependencies, and no GPL editor source remain locked. Broad UI/E2E at the final stage; focused correctness checks continue.

# Agent rules

Read [OWNER-DIRECTIVES.md](OWNER-DIRECTIVES.md) first. It overrides conflicting
roadmap and tooling text. Follow the active `work/WO-*.md`; inspect its allowed
and protected paths before editing. Keep each work order buildable, tested,
verified, and recorded in `STATE.md` and the ledgers.

## Platform and product locks

- Initial support is Apple Silicon macOS 13+. Do not add Linux/Windows code,
  shims, CI jobs, runners, packaging, or portability work.
- Keep platform implementations behind `platform/` interfaces; do not add
  stubs for unsupported operating systems.
- Rust for all first-party code is the active owner-approved migration target.
  MPL-2.0, minimal pinned dependencies, custom-drawn UI, and an owned SVG
  parser/rasterizer remain locked. Legacy C17 code is preserved as migration
  reference; do not resume old C implementation orders. See ADR-0022.
- Never read, fetch, or copy GPL SVG-editor source. Do not fetch external SVG
  resources from the application. Record provenance for external algorithms.

## Repository map

- `app/`: executable composition.
- `src/`: base, platform, XML/SVG, scene, raster, document, UI modules as added.
- `docs/research-r4/`: authoritative operating model and roadmap.
- `docs/research-r3/plan/`: architecture and coding guidance where r4 is silent.
- `docs/adr/`: accepted decisions; `work/`: immutable ready work orders.
- `tests/`: unit, property, fuzz, UI, and oracle tests as introduced.
- `bench/`: corpus metadata, generators, runners, and results.
- `artifacts/`: work-order evidence; `build/` and `.cache/` are generated.

## Commands

The commands below are the preserved legacy C workflow. Rust workspace/build
commands become authoritative only through their implementation orders.

- `./dev build`: configure and build Debug.
- `./dev test-fast`: run local Python tests and validate the ledger.
- `./dev verify`: run the Debug build and fast tests.
- `cmake --preset mac-release && cmake --build --preset mac-release`: Release.
- `python3 scripts/ledger.py validate ledger.jsonl`: validate work history.
- `python3 -m unittest`: run Python harness tests when present.
- `bench`, `fmt`, `lint`, `asan`, and `fuzz` become authoritative only when
  their work orders implement them; do not claim missing commands run.

## Engineering and safety

Use the contracts in `docs/CODING_STANDARD.md`: explicit ownership, pointer+length
slices, checked size arithmetic, bounded user input, no VLAs, and no unsafe
string functions. Preserve unknown SVG/XML source. Keep generated files in
ignored repo-local directories. Do not install system packages or touch sibling
directories. Add dependencies only through an ADR and pinned provenance record.

Never weaken frozen acceptance tests or oracles. Run commands named by the
active work order, then report exact evidence. Do not invent test or performance
results. Keep source files focused and under 800 lines; split cohesive modules
before they grow further.

## Rust migration execution

Follow `docs/product/rust-port-goal-and-plan.md` and ready Rust work orders.
Multiple Luna codex exec processes are authorized, with isolated current-source
worktrees and disjoint modules; coordinator alone changes shared manifests,
locks, interfaces and ledgers. Use Low for inventory/docs, Medium for routine
ports, High for parser/renderer/concurrency/unsafe FFI. Escalate only on a named
problem; use the existing subscription allowance and no purchased credits.
Preserve strict validation, original fixtures/assertions and byte-preserving
round trips. Rust ownership replaces manual C ownership conventions; bounded
inputs, checked arithmetic, safe cleanup and source limits still apply. Keep
unsafe operations behind documented platform/FFI boundaries.

# Goal
Produce actionable complete Rust interfaces and dependency-ready port partitions
for ALL remaining owned SVG scene/decoder/paint/clip/effects/media and scalar
raster kernels, preserving the full vector/cartoon/MCP/large-file product goal.
This is a contract plan only; it must unblock code, not select an external SVG
renderer, omit supported legacy behaviors or shrink the application.

# Files allowed to touch
- `work/WO-RUST-RENDER-CONTRACT-PLAN-01.md` (coordinator freeze only)
- `artifacts/WO-RUST-RENDER-CONTRACT-PLAN-01/**`
- `docs/product/rust-render-contract-plan.md`
- `STATE.md`, `LEDGER.md`, `ledger.jsonl`, `docs/product/rust-port-goal-and-plan.md` (coordinator only)

# Required work and bounded research
Read OWNER-DIRECTIVES/AGENTS/ADR0022/23/24/25/coding standard, accepted Rust
contracts (geometry/path/values/color/CSS/reference/XML/animation/raster/spatial/
tile/task/document) and existing rendering research. Source inventory is
src/svg/shape (including .h/internal/alloc/media/custom/selection/document),
svg/paint/clip, remaining src/raster shape_* and injected macOS media headers.
Discover every named source file; inspect public/internal headers, include
edges and function signatures, then only implementation excerpts needed to
resolve ownership/dependencies/errors/work/memory contracts. Do not dump/read
whole trees, old logs or whole huge sources gratuitously.
Map every remaining C implementation to exactly one full port or explain an
already accepted replacement with symbol evidence. Resolve shape/paint/clip/
pattern/mask recursive dependencies through owned data and explicit operations,
not stub functions, fake providers, duplicate shadow parsers or self-references.
Propose minimal crate/module layout, complete shared type/API signatures,
source Arc/spans/cached tables, bound/capacity/error/diagnostic contracts,
media ownership/drop/thread requirements, cancellation/work charging and frozen
read/write interfaces. Preserve exact supported feature breadth, unsupported
reports, paint order, fill/stroke/effects/math operation order, source/transform/
path metadata and scalar rendering fidelity. No new unsafe except later audited
native boundary, no new dependencies, external SVG fetch, GPL editor source,
unsupported OS or speculative SIMD/GPU rewrite. C kernels are the migration
reference; paper directions remain testable inferences.

Identify hard accepted-contract gaps (for example owned animation views without
cloning/reparsing) separately with minimal additive API changes; do not consume
unaccepted editor/native candidates. Provide viable disjoint writers after
shared contracts land, one owner per module and coordinator-only composition.
Any implementation partition must contain its entire named C/API scope and
original meaningful assertions; do not create convenient smaller renderer.
Map required original focused suites/fixtures/limits to each port and preserve
24 frozen authored goldens and existing raster/oracle tests for their respective
acceptance stage. Final broad UI/E2E/corpus/performance/release/live demos remain
explicit. Large100MB editing/rendering/save and budgets remain full product
requirements even where old parity entry points have16MiB defaults.

# Protected paths and verification
All product/peer code, other docs/orders/artifacts/manifests/locks and index/HEAD/
original603legacy. Own report/evidence only; no source, Cargo, ledger edits by
worker, dependencies/network/install/builds/tests/recursive agents/commit/stage/
reset/delete. Actual Standard subscription Sol6.1Medium, narrow cross-file
architecture scope; no purchasedcredits/APIbilling, stop allowanceerrors.

# Output
Concise report<=2000words, machine-readable complete per-file/symbol ownership
matrix, dependency DAG, signatures/contracts/limits/error/source/thread data,
original assertion assignments, implementation launch order and exact proof
commands. Result<=350words. Every omitted or unresolved feature is explicit;
no application, renderer or performance acceptance claim. Coordinator freezes
implementation scopes and registration after review.

# ADR0022: Full first-party Rust port

- Status: accepted (language/scope/owner direction; detailed stack pending research)
- Date:2026-10-14
- Decision owner: project owner

The owner stopped the C implementation and requested a full Rust port, internet
research and maximum useful parallel Luna codex exec execution. Rust supersedes
ADR0001 language/build decision; no shipped first-party C/Objective-C backend is
the finish line. Platform interfaces and system macOS frameworks remain.
Application, custom UI, owned XML/SVG/rasterizer, document/project/recovery,
animation, MCP, developer tools and test harnesses all belong in the port.
Existing C code/candidates/tests/evidence are retained as migration references.

ADR0018 complete product scope and final software acceptance+recorded
Codex character/animation demonstration remain required. macOS13+ AppleSilicon,
MPL2, source preservation, no external SVG fetching, minimal reviewed/pinned
dependencies and no GPL editor source remain locked. Broad UI/E2E stays final.
Rust toolchain/crate choices follow six scoped primary-source research reports
and separate ready implementation orders; no speed, memory or size superiority
is presumed without measured parity evidence.
# ADR0023: Rust foundation workspace

Accepted2026-10-14 under the full-port owner direction. Rust1.99.0/2024/resolver3,
MPL2, std-only/internal dependencies, macOS13 AppleSilicon only. Base/geometry/
xml/json/project/raster and developer CLI members are scaffolding for ports.
Domain crates forbid unsafe; native FFI belongs to a later audited platform crate.
No external dependency adoption. Shared Span(start,end) uses checked arithmetic
and slices. Point/Affine are f64 SVG geometry, compose maps right first.
Coordinator owns manifests/lock/contracts. Build success is not product parity.

Exact compiler pin1.99.0 is recorded. The host stable alias resolves to it, so
checks use +stable after exact-version verification without global installs.
Build/cache/tmp output repo-local. Six disjoint foundation owners port modules
behind these interfaces, with focused checks and original fixture preservation.
# ADR0024: Rust native system services boundary

Accepted2026-10-14 for macOS13 AppleSilicon native services only. No external
crate or first-party C shim. Rust safe wrappers encapsulate tiny audited unsafe
FFI module, crate deny unsafe plus allow only sys and deny unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn.
ABI types/prototypes checked against local SDK headers and primary docs; foreign
functions borrow buffers/fds only synchronously. No unsupported OS implementation.

Services: Apple Security SecRandomCopyBytes using documented NULL default
provider, bounded<=256bytes, check returned status and clear output on failure;
getuid and getpeereid through System with u32 uid/gid, BorrowedFd and immediate
errno capture. Test actual OS success and pure failure classification without
faking native security certification. Other platform/window/file/graphics/AX
services remain future scopes; AppKit dependency choices not adopted here.

Primary sources fetched2026-10-14:
- https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/ffi.html
- https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/secrandomcopybytes(_:_:_:)
- https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/ksecrandomdefault
- https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/getpeereid.3.html
Apple Markdown establishes availabilitymacOS10.7 and defaultconstant=NULL;
getentropy localman recommends Security for clients needing random bytes.
API facts only, no external algorithm/editor source copied.
# ADR0025: consuming Darwin checked close for atomic saves

Status: accepted2026-10-14. Scope: Apple Silicon macOS13+, platform boundary only.
This resolves WO-RUST-ATOMIC-FILES-01 r1 std-only blocker; it does not approve a
new dependency, Cshim, OS target or weakened publication/durability behavior.

Rust File Drop ignores close errors. Owned C atomic operations check close before
rename/link commit. Preserve that observable error contract with one tiny private
Darwin binding, alongside existing Security/System bindings in sys.rs:
close(int)->int, SDK unistd.h declaration line449 inspected locally.

Safe public signature: close_checked(OwnedFd)->std::io::Result<()>. Convert File
with its safe owned conversion. sys consumes the descriptor using IntoRawFd,
performs exactly one synchronous close, checks result, captures errno immediately
on failure and returns an owned IO error. No public raw pointer/descriptor API,
no double drop, blind close retry or resurrection of consumed ownership. This
matches the existing C close_checked policy, which clears its descriptor before
calling close. No claim of platform-independent EINTR semantics is introduced.

All unsafe stays in tiny private sys.rs with individual SAFETY ABI/ownership/
no-retention comments; crate deny unsafe and unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn remain. Keep
accepted entropy/getuid/getpeereid bodies/tests intact. Atomic file operations
and typed safe hooks stay outside the unsafe module. Close errors before commit
must prevent rename/publication; postcommit directory durability errors report
published state accurately. Tests cover actual consuming native success and
safe error classification/precommit close failure seam without forged invalid
OwnedFd, secrets or synthetic native failure claims. Cleanup closes temporary
handles exactly once and never publishes after a precommit failure.

Primary references checked2026-10-14 (facts only, no source copied):
- [Rust File close/Drop behavior](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/struct.File.html)
- [Rust OwnedFd ownership/conversions](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/os/fd/struct.OwnedFd.html)
- [Apple close return/error contract](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/close.2.html)
- Installed Apple SDK usr/include/unistd.h close(int) declaration.
# C17 coding standard

This document is normative. Changes to ABI, ownership, threading, or source
preservation require an ADR.

## Names and structure

- Use C17, four-space indentation, LF, and `snake_case` identifiers.
- Prefix exported symbols with their module (`svg_`, `ui_`, `raster_`).
- Keep public contracts in headers and module ownership/tests in a short README.
- Prefer small functions with early error returns. Comments explain invariants,
  units, lifetime, and non-obvious choices.
- Keep source files below 800 lines; split modules before they grow further.

## Ownership and memory

- State whether each pointer is owned or borrowed and how long it stays valid.
- Use pointer+length slices; never infer length from a missing terminator.
- Use arenas or module allocators. Avoid allocation in hot loops.
- Check addition, multiplication, and capacity growth before allocation.
- Do not use VLAs, `alloca`, `strcpy`, `strcat`, `sprintf`, or unchecked format
  construction. No implicit null-termination assumptions.
- Do not retain pointers into growable buffers or pass unowned pointers between
  threads. OOM must not leave a partial edit committed.

## Errors, parsing, and assertions

- Malformed input, resource limits, unsupported features, and OOM are normal
  errors, not assertions.
- Assertions document impossible internal invariants only.
- Bound bytes, nodes, nesting, expansion, pixels, and work queues.
- Never load network resources or execute SVG scripts. Preserve unknown source
  spans and namespaces.
- Define behavior for overflow, NaN/Inf, invalid matrices, malformed UTF-8,
  invalid path flags, and zero divisors.
- Avoid recursion over user-controlled depth unless an explicit depth budget is
  checked.

## Concurrency and rendering

- Mutate documents on the UI thread. Workers read immutable snapshots and
  publish owned results tagged with a generation.
- Cancel, drain, and join workers before releasing snapshots or source buffers.
- Scalar rendering is deterministic and is the reference for optimized paths.
- Keep allocation out of pixel loops and record performance counters at module
  boundaries.

## Verification

Use only build, test, sanitizer, fuzz, format, lint, and benchmark commands
implemented by the active work order. Run required checks explicitly and record
their results. Benchmarks must include machine, compiler, build type, workload,
and raw measurements. Never claim a speedup without a reproducible baseline.
# Scientific evidence for Vexel rendering and responsiveness

Date: 2026-10-14. Work order: WO-RUST-RESEARCH-SCIENCE-01.
Requested skill: `science-paper-search`. This is a targeted literature review
for rendering, parsing resource bounds, and interaction latency within the
existing full Rust product goal. It does not establish performance gains or
complete the renderer, editor, native UI, or live MCP integration.

## Search and evidence

Used the free unauthenticated ScienceMadeReadable/OpenAlex route. The web tool
could not open its guide; the bundled standard-library helper fetched the
current guide successfully. All eight API requests returned HTTP200, including
five searches, one similarity expansion and one citation walk, plus the guide.
Requests were sequential and spaced beyond2.1seconds. No account, server
registration, credits, dependency, or private project information was submitted.

Queries searched GPU vector/path rasterization (semantic and exact terms),
bounded incremental XML, and input-feedback latency, then expanded the2016
scanline seed with similarity/citation queries. An exact inking-title search
checked publication versions. Raw timestamped request/response envelopes,
`query-log.json`, `screened-records.json`, `version-reconciliation.json` and
hashed primary PDFs/text extractions are in the work-order artifacts.

The index covers titles/abstracts, not full papers. This is not an exhaustive
survey or a ranking-based algorithm decision. Some exact-word results concerned
vectorization, neural generation or3D rendering and were excluded as different
tasks. Citation walking suggested silhouette texture magnification; that is
outside the present SVG editing scope. No external implementation was copied,
no GPL editor source was read, and code licenses were not established: any
future adoption needs separate provenance/dependency review.

## Relevant primary evidence

Full texts were obtained for the first five entries below; methods,
experimental setup, evaluation and limitations relevant to Vexel were examined,
rather than claiming every section was reviewed. The final entry remains a
retrieved abstract shortlist because its author endpoint failed TLS hostname
verification; certificate checks were retained.

| Paper | What the evidence supports | Limits for Vexel |
|---|---|---|
| [Nehab & Hoppe, Random-access rendering of general vector graphics (2008)](https://hhoppe.com/ravg.pdf) | Cell-local descriptions reduce work to spatially relevant primitives; extended cell regions support filtering. The paper explicitly discusses static-layout/re-encoding and unsupported-attribute limitations. | DirectX10/GeForce8800GTX, not AppleMetal. Include preprocessing, replicated storage, edit invalidation, thin strokes and corner quality in comparisons. |
| [Ganacim et al., Massively-parallel vector graphics (2014)](https://w3.impa.br/~diego/publications/GanEtAl14.pdf) | A shortcut-tree pipeline parallelizes preprocessing by segment and rendering by sample/pixel. Evaluations use a GTXTitan and report preprocessing separately from rendering. | Old GPU/hardware and selected vector illustrations. Raster timings alone do not establish editor latency, SVG fidelity or whole-frame rebuild cost. |
| [Konrad & Magniez, Validating XML Documents in the Streaming Model with External Memory (arXiv1012.3311)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.3311) | General DTD validation has space/pass trade-offs; the external-memory algorithm uses additional streams and passes. | The downloaded revision is2021; initial preprint2010, with later conference/journal versions. This is DTD validation, not our lexical source-preserving parser or editable DOM. It does not prove constant-memory editing. |
| [Ng et al., Designing for low-latency direct-touch input (UIST2012)](https://www.tactuallabs.com/papers/designingLowLatencyDirectTouchInputUIST12.pdf) | Ten right-handed participants compared direct-touch dragging delays on special low-latency hardware. The paper proposes immediate simple feedback followed by detailed visuals. | The experiment measures perceptual discrimination during touch dragging. It does not establish Vexel or general application performance, or macOS mouse/tablet productivity. Low-millisecond observations are not universal acceptance thresholds. |
| [Annett et al., How Low Should We Go? (Graphics Interface2014)](https://webdocs.cs.ualberta.ca/~wfb/publications/C-2014-GI-Latency.pdf) | Writing/sketching with a custom stylus system produced different perceptual thresholds from simpler dragging. The first experiment uses12 participants and examines just-noticeable differences. | Perception differs from tolerance and task completion. The indexed2020 chapter is treated as a related version, not another replication. No blanket50ms product threshold follows. |
| [Li, Hou & Zhou, Efficient GPU path rendering using scanline rasterization (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1145/2980179.2982434) | Retrieved abstract describes boundary-fragment work and bulk interior spans. This is an abstract-only lead for later primary-source review, with no recommendation. | Full author PDF unavailable in this run. Reported speedups are not verified here or transferable to AppleSilicon. |

## Testable implementation directions

These are engineering inferences from the evidence, not measured Vexel results.

1. **Retain spatially local rendering and bounded caching.** Keep source/vector
   data editable and preserved. Evaluate coarse tile/cell culling and local
   invalidation; measure overlap amplification and cache metadata as well as
   pixels. Compare against the owned CPU renderer before choosing a Metal path.
2. **Include every stage in animation costs.** Measure decoding, path expansion,
   spatial preprocessing, invalidation, rendering and presentation separately
   and together. Use both static pan/zoom and changing artwork/timeline input;
   caching a static illustration cannot establish animated-frame performance.
3. **Separate progress from validation.** A partial preview must not certify an
   unvalidated document. Keep bounded per-step work, cancellation and explicit
   storage errors; charge actual reserved token/table capacity. Streaming
   visitors and retained editable models have different memory requirements.
4. **Measure feedback by task and input.** Record input-to-first-visible-feedback
   and input-to-final-frame for drawing, dragging/nodes, pan/zoom, playback and
   live MCP transactions. Fast previews must converge to faithful output and
   visibly report transaction/progress/cancel state, preserving undo integrity.
5. **Preserve existing product budgets.** ADR0018’s100MB/2second first-content,
   <100ms owner-thread pause and p95<33ms pan/zoom targets remain unchanged.
   Later work orders must name AppleSilicon hardware/OS/build, corpus hashes,
   cold/warm protocol, repeated p50/p95/worst samples and memory/quality results.
   Record end-to-end latency separately from renderer duration. No new broad
   UI/performance suite ran during this research.

## Gaps and next evidence

AppleMetal equivalence, full SVG clips/masks/text/effects, dynamic source editing,
MCP transaction observability and representative-user measurements remain open.
The review does not select an external renderer or retire the owned parser.
Native animation authoring and Rust/AppKit integration still follow the full
product plan. Comprehensive UI/E2E, fidelity, performance, accessibility,

item.text: Two shared API gaps need review before implementation: animation owns track vectors but borrows source, and the values attribute adapter rejects containing sources above 16 MiB. I’m recording minimal additive contracts for both. To break the pattern decode/raster cycle, I’m defining an explicit continuation that renders a completed child scene and returns its tile to the decoder.

/bin/zsh -lc "cat > docs/product/rust-render-contract-plan.md <<'EOF'
# Rust renderer contract and port plan

WO-RUST-RENDER-CONTRACT-PLAN-01, revision 1. **Proposal for independent review;
implementation scopes and registrations must be frozen by root afterward.**
This plan changes no application code and claims no renderer, application,
fidelity, memory, or performance acceptance.

Owner directives, AGENTS, ADR0022–25, the coding standard, accepted Rust package
checkpoints, named C public/internal headers and signatures, and the existing
rendering research govern this proposal. Legacy README limits are stale where
current headers/signatures differ. Research directions remain testable
inferences; the C kernels remain the operation-order reference. No external
renderer, dependency, native binding candidate, or source-editor candidate is
adopted. Initial support remains Apple Silicon macOS13+, MPL2 and owned SVG/XML.

## Complete ownership and evidence

Evidence is in [the work-order artifact directory](../../artifacts/WO-RUST-RENDER-CONTRACT-PLAN-01/).
The machine files are normative proposal details, beyond this concise report:

- "'`source-api-inventory.json`: every file in `src/svg/shape`, `svg/paint`,
  `svg/clip`, `raster/shape_*`, and injected `platform/media`; signatures,
  include edges, original macros and source hashes. Native animation export is
  explicitly accounted downstream.
- `ownership-matrix.json`: **69 files and 678 signature locations**, including
  private helpers, header declarations and forward declarations. Each location
  has one owner, target module and disposition. Locations are not 678 distinct
  public APIs. Whole-file scope includes cleanup, custom geometry, source
  selection, allocation hooks, metadata, unsupported errors and diagnostics.
- `accepted-api-signatures.json`: main-tree accepted public API evidence.
  `accepted-contract-gaps.json` separates proposed additions from accepted APIs.
- `shared-contracts.json`: shared data, typed operations, actual ownership,
  read/write boundaries, continuation requests and failure behavior.
- `limits-features.json`: 140 original macro definitions, 90 resolved limits,
  scalar/math/error contracts and explicit supported/unsupported feature scope.
- `dependency-dag.json`: partition prerequisites, disjoint writers and launch
  order. `assertion-assignments.json` binds 53 original suite/support files,
  1,458 assertion/condition locations, 104 fixtures and all 24 authored goldens.

The scope preserves all path commands, basic/rounded geometry, source-number
and command/subpath provenance, CSS/currentColor, root/nested/symbol viewports,
use instances, switch language conditionals, inherited styles, complete paint,
clip, marker, pattern, mask, filter, media and explicit-time composition.
Bounds, scanline/event trees, uniform fill intervals/runs, dash/seam/join caches,
stroke grids, conservative boundary marking, work preflight, scalar sampling,
flat/grouped rendering and original measurement/oracle adapters remain full
ports. A helper'"'s privacy never removes its behavior or assertions.

## Shared ownership and cycles

Four new internal crate roles suffice: "'`vexel-scene` for shared owned data and
contracts, `vexel-svg-decode` for decoding/resolution, `vexel-svg-scalar` for the
full scalar kernels, and `vexel-svg-render` for coordinator composition.
These are proposed registrations, not edits to Cargo.

A graph owns the accepted `Arc<Vec<u8>>` source lease, scene tables, masks,
materialized patterns, clips and animation data. Source bytes are never copied
for nested definitions. Checked base/XML spans retain original offsets.
Instance-specific transform frames keep attribute, suffix, motion and parent;
path tables retain authored case, implicit commands and explicit stroke closure.
Sparse fill/stroke paints, shared dash values and per-edge colors/shape IDs remain.
Masks refer to completed child scene IDs; clips use validated arena IDs and
parent links. The graph admits no ownership back edges. Active definition
identity/depth/instance checks reject recursive expansion normally.

Source and token owners live outside the decoder. Its temporary CSS/reference
objects borrow those owners; neither an owned scene nor decoder embeds a
self-reference. Endpoint/attribute/paint/text caches are bounded and die with
decode. Persisted tables contain checked spans/IDs and owned Rust buffers.
Builder transactions reserve before mutation and roll back every coupled table;
work already performed is not refunded. Published scenes expose immutable
views. Mutable access exists only in builder transactions and owned evaluated
frame tables.

The decoder suspends at the original pattern-render point and emits a ticket
plus a completed child view. Composition invokes the actual full scalar kernel,
then returns the owned tile through `resume_pattern`. Nested patterns complete
first. The ticket is consumed once; failure aborts the draft. This preserves
error order and avoids a decoder-to-raster crate cycle, duplicate parsing,
self-referencing providers, placeholder tiles or omitted pattern strokes.

Definition planners return typed expansions/postoperations; only the traversal
engine walks them. Shared `DecodeOperations` signatures permit independent
compilation; coordinator bridges delegate complete paint/definition/media
implementations. The real flat kernel similarly implements `FlatKernel` for
full grouped rendering. Neither interface permits production scope to be
replaced with a convenient smaller renderer. There are no temporary stub bodies
or unfinished peer implementation dependencies.

Clip decoding uses original token ranges with restricted clip flavor and
clip-rule inheritance, replacing synthetic wrapper decoding. Original admission
limits and diagnostic offsets remain; actual allocation counters measure actual
buffers, rather than invented wrapper allocations. Queries retain child union,
parent intersection and conservative boundary behavior when inversion fails.

## Contracts that must land first

Four additive gates require independent review and root-owned implementation:

1. **Owned animation/view:** accepted `Document` borrows source and owns track
   vectors. Move parsed vectors into an owned source lease and expose borrowed
   slices to the same evaluator. No cloned tracks, reparsing or parallel parser.
2. **Large values adapter:** accepted containing-source checks are 16MiB and
   attribute views cap at256. Add policy-bearing entry points up to1GiB/4096
   attributes without changing existing defaults, grammar or absolute offsets.
   No source-slice shortcut disguises a smaller decoder limit.
3. **Existing parser/flatten access:** expose the accepted number/length cursor
   and curve/edge operations needed for primitive/text/custom geometry. Reuse
   accepted path output with checked table rebasing; do not port shadow readers.
4. **Controlled work/capacity:** shared base control and additive CSS/reference/
   path/animation APIs expose cancellation, actual reserved bytes and real
   resumable cursor state. Existing one-shot entry points use the same engine.
   `Pending` reports actual charged work and cannot certify success.

The task queue'"'s scalar completion API remains accepted as-is: an owned job
context uses a separately bounded result slot/channel keyed by task/generation;
"'`TaskOutput` signals completion. No assumed typed tile-return API is invented.
The accepted document model supplies the source lease and source ranges;
composition does not depend on unfinished editor snapshot interfaces.
Accepted spatial queries and tile cache ownership/epoch/capacity APIs remain the
integration seams for visible work and invalidation. Published results carry a
generation; stale/canceled results are dropped. Drain/join precedes lease release.

## Media, limits and fidelity

Media injection remains synchronous and real. Requests borrow UTF8/encoded
bytes only until return; outputs own Rust text outlines or premultiplied RGBA
buffers. The provider need not cross threads. Framework handles must be
released on the invoking thread before owned Rust outputs are transferred;
no foreign pointer/release token survives in the graph. Later native orders
must audit actual CoreText/CoreGraphics/ImageIO ABI, ownership, availability,
threading and failure/drop paths. Unaccepted binding research is not a usable
implementation. Missing text/image service reports original unsupported errors,
never successful fake media. Original deterministic injected tests remain tests.

Charge actual reserved capacity, including source lease capacity once, token
and open-name storage, lookup/cache metadata, all scene/overlay/media buffers
and overlapping nested group/mask/filter scratch. All range/size arithmetic is
checked; fallible reserve occurs before commit. Bounds and admission caps keep
the original per-scene versus job-wide semantics and nested shared counters.
Native synchronous calls are cancellation boundaries with bounded inputs;
Rust work checks cancellation at bounded intervals. Unsafe belongs only to a
later separately audited native boundary; domain code adds none.

Current source/token bounds are1GiB/256MiB, edges4,194,304, shapes65,536,
commands4,194,304. The native-resolution preflight remains
`min(16,000,000,000, 200,000,000 + max(0,pixels-1,048,576)*24,576)`.
Group/filter scratch remains64MiB with shared occupancy, and filters retain50M
work. Grid/fill ineligibility keeps original scalar fallbacks, not refusal.
The machine matrix preserves the remaining exact caps, including differing SVG
and native per-run/document text budgets.

Preserve f64 operation order, right-first transforms, clipping inequalities,
sort ties, alpha numerators/rounding, gradient/image/pattern interpolation,
4x4 subpixel locations, blur passes and linear/sRGB conversions. Group order is
children, filter, mask, opacity/blend. Oracle-only synthetic alpha stays test-only.
No FMA reassociation, SIMD/GPU rewrite, source normalization or changed goldens.

Unsupported filter categories remain distinct. External resources/scripts,
textPath, color-only glyphs, animated image input and original restricted
CSS/clip/pattern forms retain their reports. Current animated geometry/effect/
pattern and active path-composition restrictions remain explicit; broader
product authoring workflows are downstream work, not claimed implemented.

## Execution and acceptance

Root first reviews/freezes shared interfaces and additive gates, then registers
modules. Disjoint decoder, paint, definition, SVG media, scene-query/accounting,
raster-index, raster-sample and animation writers can proceed against frozen
contracts. Definitions alone own lower clip queries; paint alone owns lower
paint sampling. Raster effects and audited native media follow, then coordinator
composition and complete native export. One writer owns each module; root alone
changes shared interfaces/manifests/locks/orders/ledgers. No worker was launched.

Each partition receives its entire named C/API scope and original meaningful
suite assertions. Full scalar integration owns mixed suites, random byte
comparisons, exact budget/error counters and all24 frozen authored goldens;
actual native media is mandatory at that stage. No weaker tolerances, reduced
fixtures or re-generated baselines are authorized. Future orders must freeze
focused Rust proof commands after registration. No hypothetical command is
reported as executed here.

Full100MB editing/rendering/save, first content<2s, owner pauses<100ms and cached
pan/zoom p95<33ms remain product requirements. Resumable/visible work is required;
a partial preview cannot certify final validation. Module limits are not proof
of those budgets. Broad UI/E2E, full corpus/fuzz/fidelity/performance, native
accessibility/recovery, packaging/release and authentic live MCP vector/cartoon
recordings remain final gates.

Executed proof commands are the work order'"'s ready validator, ledger validator
and "'`git diff --check`; exact results are in `validators.json`. Worker observation
found HEAD/index unchanged and one protected source-editor candidate delta
relative to the existing launch baseline. No attribution or original603/root
preservation acceptance is asserted. Independent review, root preservation
audit, implementation freeze and registration remain pending.
EOF'
